text:
maria: Heads up — ap-southeast1 scratch pool started returning GPU attach failures overnight. Alerts show a scrub IOPS ramp at ~03:00 and a bunch of nvme CRC/read errors.

ops-bot: Alert: GPU-attach-timeout ap-southeast1 — 5 hosts failing (automated)

tom: Any kernel logs we can look at?

maria: Pasted partial /var/log/messages from one affected host:

```
kernel: nvme0: background scrub start
kernel: nvme0: controller 0000:3b:00:0: scrub: completed sector CRC -5
kernel: nvme0: aio read failed -110
kernel: nvme0: device temporarily unavailable; failing probe for local volume
gk-resolver: attach timeout=120s pod=gpu-worker-xx -> mount failed
```

jin: Huh. Scrub shouldn't produce CRCs normally. Did we roll firmware recently?

maria: Yes — firmware-deploy bot rolled v2.1.8 to ap-southeast1 around 02:40 last night. infra-bot posted the deploy.

infra-bot: firmware-deploy v2.1.8 completed to ap-southeast1 (canary 3 nodes, 48 nodes total)

tom: New firmware + concurrent scrub could be interacting with controller error paths and causing transient device read failures/timeouts. We've seen similar when scrub IO hits a controller bug.

maria: Current impact: ~6% of scratch nodes go readonly or fail attach; GPU provisioning falls back to dedicated pool for ~12% of requests which is pressuring capacity. Preemptible pool usage jumped.

sam: Customers seeing increased latency for inference requests — new tail latencies from queued jobs. What's the short plan?

jin: Quick mitigations I propose:
1) Throttle janitor scrub IOPS to 2–5% for ap-southeast1 immediately
2) Cordon + selectively drain the worst offenders (limit to a few nodes to avoid big churn)
3) Reschedule full scrubs to midday for the next 48h
4) Prepare rollback to fw v2.1.7 if errors continue after throttling

tom: +1 to throttling first. Draining will shift pods and cause more dedicated fallback, so cost + capacity tradeoff. Estimate ~20 node drains -> ~$1200/day extra infra if sustained.

maria: Running the throttle now, issuing cordon for top offenders. Commands I'm using:

```bash
# throttle scrub iops to a conservative cap for ap-southeast1
kubectl -n ops exec janitor-0 -- ./janitorctl set-scrub-rate --pool=ap-southeast1-scratch --iops=2000

# cordon & drain one of the worst nodes (doing this slowly)
kubectl cordon gnode-ap-sg-045
kubectl drain gnode-ap-sg-045 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

infra-bot: janitorctl: scrub rate set to 2000 IOPS for ap-southeast1-scratch (effective immediately)

ops-bot: Node cordon gnode-ap-sg-045 succeeded; drain started (pods being rescheduled)

maria: Monitoring metrics — disk iops dropped ~65% within 10m, attach errors reduced from ~6/min to ~1/min after ~12m. GPU attach failures fell from 8% -> 3% in the same window.

jin: If errors keep dropping we keep throttle for 24h and stagger scrub windows. I'll open TICKET-7834 to track rollback, trace artifacts, and cost impact analysis.

sam: Rescheduling scrub windows to 11:00-14:00 for next 48h to avoid overnight batch workloads. Noted.

tom: Follow-ups (post-incident):
- collect kernel traces and nvme SMART/health for affected nodes
- vendor engagement: ask NVMe vendor for CRC/firmware interaction explanation
- add a canary/ramp for scrub when firmware changes land (e.g., incremental IOPS ramp)

maria: On it — I'll attach traces to TICKET-7834 and leave the throttle in place until we complete vendor triage. Thanks all :thumbsup:

infra-bot: Incident INC-2026 created and linked to TICKET-7834 for tracking
